text:
Maria: heads-up for Apr 14 webinar: we need a compact benchmark artifact (for keynote slide + social). thinking a split layout: left = unit economics (cost/1k tokens) with throughput as secondary axis, right = p95 latency at 512 tokens across tiers (Hosted / Dedicated / Private). can someone sketch copy + data?

Alyssa: i can do copy. want the headline to be value-first: 'Know the cost. Control the latency.' short subhead: 'Same API. Pick the economics that match your SLOs.'

Ian: i'll prep the data plot. prefer showing absolute $ and small % badges for delta vs redwood-3b baseline. Also recommend showing a small legend explaining caching on/off.

perf-bot: uploaded dataset: s3://redwood-perf/benchmarks/mini_launch_512_2026-03-21.csv. contains: model, tier, p50,p95,p99,throughput_rps,cost_per_1k,caching_enabled.

Kate: design asks: please keep colors WCAG-friendly, use patterns for bars for accessibility, and keep axis labels large enough for slide. avoid busy gridlines.

Lina: inbound CTA idea: small inline estimator on blog + modal on the webinar landing page. CTA text variants: (A) 'Estimate your cost' -> leads to estimator; (B) 'Talk to an architect' -> Dedicated/Private consult. map responses to lead tags: estimator->MQL, architect->SQL. Sales-bot: mapped.

Sales-bot: routing: estimator -> tag:bench_estimator, score:5; architect -> tag:bench_architect, score:50. Hidden field: "expected_annual_spend" added.

Maria: good. Ian, can you drop a CSV preview here? want numbers to call out that Dedicated has the lowest p95 but higher $/1k; Hosted is cheaper per token for most models but slightly higher p95.

Ian: sample rows:

```csv
model,tier,throughput_rps,p50_ms,p95_ms,cost_per_1k,caching_enabled
redwood-3b,Hosted,140,30,62,0.10,true
redwood-13b,Hosted,68,22,70,0.22,false
redwood-13b,Dedicated,120,18,38,0.30,false
redwood-rtq-13b,Hosted,80,25,55,0.16,true
llama-2-13b,Private,65,20,40,0.35,false
```

Alyssa: copy for slide deck (two-liner under headline): 'We measured common generation workloads at 512-token responses. Results show predictable tradeoffs: Dedicated for tight latency SLOs, Hosted for cost-efficiency, Private for data-sensitive deployments.'

Ian: visualization notes: Panel A = grouped bars by model showing cost_per_1k (left axis) with throughput_rps as a dashed line on right axis; Panel B = stacked mini-bars showing p95 for each tier colored by tier. Add small callouts pointing to caching cases with % reduction.

Kate: will make small callout stickers: 'Caching enabled -> up to 40% lower token cost' and 'Fallbacks to smaller models can cut cost by ~25% with modest latency increase.'

Lina: for the blog/social intro: short hook + 1 bullet list: why this matters (predictable infra costs, fast failover, same API). social variants: long (LinkedIn) and short (X).

Alyssa: rough social copy drafts:

X (short): 'We benchmarked LLM serving across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. Tradeoffs are clear: Dedicated = lowest p95, Hosted = lowest $/1k. Same API. Choose based on SLOs. Try our cost estimator -> <link>'

LinkedIn (long): 'How do you balance latency and cost when serving LLMs? We ran a set of production-like benchmarks at 512 tokens. Results: Dedicated hardware delivers the best latency, Hosted gives the best cost-per-token for most model choices, and Private gives predictable isolation. Read the full breakdown and try the estimator.'

Maria: accessibility + compliance head's up: call out that Private tier numbers are from our private deployment testbed and may vary for customer-managed infra. also add a small privacy badge on the slide when we talk about Private.

Ian: pushing a first-pass PNGs to #marketing-assets by 3:30pm. will include tiny table under charts with raw numbers. Kate: use brand fonts and patterns.

Kate: noted. will start layout and keep both square (for social) and 16:9 (for keynote).

Alyssa: action items recap: copy (me) by 1:30pm; visuals (Ian + Kate) first pass by 3:30pm; landing CTA wiring (Lina) by 5pm; sales routing confirmed (Sales-bot) done. Maria: i'll ping product/legal if needed.

Maria: perfect. one extra ask: can we include a one-sentence 'how we measured' footnote: 'All tests run on the same model weights with Redwood runtime optimizations; caching and batching configured per-usage profile.' keep it short.

Ian: adding that as a small footnote. also planning to export CSVs for the blog so readers can reproduce.

Kate: posting draft assets to #marketing-assets in 2h.

perf-bot: scheduled re-run for rtq quant profile at 2026-03-21T15:40Z, ETA 15m. will update CSV when complete.

Maria: thanks team. if visuals look good we'll lock by 5:30pm and hand to design for final polish. :rocket:
